category: small kitchen appliances: blenders, mixers, juicers and their accessories
status_note: Candidate set and discriminating attributes hand-built from the HS nomenclature, Chapter 85 notes and WCO GRI. CROSS/BTI references are illustrative pointers to search; verify each before citing a specific ruling number.

attributes.has_electric_motor: Does the product contain an electric motor that drives the blade?
attributes.motor_self_contained: Is the motor built into the product itself (not a separate base or kitchen machine it attaches to)?
attributes.has_heating_element: Does it heat food or liquid (e.g. soup-maker function)?
attributes.domestic_use: Is it designed for household use (not commercial/industrial food preparation)?
attributes.is_accessory_only: Is the item only a cup, jar or lid sold on its own, with no motor?

candidates.title: Electromechanical domestic appliances with self-contained electric motor: food grinders and mixers; fruit or vegetable juice extractors
candidates.reasoning: Heading 85.09 covers domestic electromechanical appliances with a self-contained motor; Chapter 85 notes include food grinders and mixers in 85.09 whatever their weight. A battery-powered portable blender is a food mixer with a self-contained motor.

candidates.title: Electro-thermic domestic appliances, other
candidates.reasoning: If the appliance heats (blender-soup maker), the heating function can give it the character of an electrothermic appliance of heading 85.16; requires GRI 3 analysis of essential character.

candidates.title: Parts of electromechanical domestic appliances of heading 85.09
candidates.reasoning: A blade/jar unit that only works when mounted on a separate motor base is classified as a part, not as a complete appliance.

candidates.title: Machinery for the industrial preparation of food or drink, other
candidates.reasoning: Commercial or industrial food-preparation machines fall outside 85.09, which is limited to domestic appliances.

candidates.title: Tableware and kitchenware, of plastics
candidates.reasoning: A plastic (e.g. Tritan) cup or jar sold on its own, with no motor, is plastic kitchenware.
